claims.text: The target eutectic high-entropy alloy has dual-phase lamellar colonies, such as an FCC/B2 structure.
Numerous internal lamellar boundaries act as crack-initiation sites and limit room-temperature tensile ductility.
A stepwise controllable process can form coherent nanoprecipitates within eutectic lamellar colonies.
Coherent nanoprecipitates will impede dislocation pile-up in the eutectic lamellar structure.
Coherent nanoprecipitates will blunt or delay microcrack initiation.
Coherent precipitate–matrix interfaces alter stress distributions at internal lamellar boundaries.
Coherent precipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission.
Coherent precipitate interfaces relieve stress concentrations that can cause premature crack initiation.
The precipitates act as well-bonded reinforcing barriers while preserving improved plastic deformation.
The intervention will increase room-temperature yield strength relative to an unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
The intervention will increase room-temperature tensile elongation relative to an unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
Stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitation has produced ultrahigh strength and ambient-temperature tensile ductility in a tungsten refractory high-entropy alloy.
The magnitude of the strength and ductility gains depends on precipitate size and distribution.
The approach is effective only when the precipitates remain coherent and are optimally dispersed.
Excessive precipitation or incoherent interfaces may cause embrittlement.
Significant alteration of lamellar-colony spacing may cause embrittlement or uneven mechanical properties.
A same-composition processed group and unmodified control group will be compared by room-temperature tensile testing and microstructural characterization.
The hypothesis is declared falsified if both yield strength and tensile ductility do not improve significantly, or if predominantly coherent nanoprecipitates are not confirmed.
